title: The use of ChatGPT as a learning tool to improve foreign language writing in a multilingual and multicultural classroom
venue: Advances in Mobile Learning Educational Research
extended_summary:
This pilot study examines whether ChatGPT can function as a feedback tool to improve foreign language writing for students with refugee/migrant backgrounds. The paper is motivated by the growing interest in generative AI for language learning and by the specific needs of socially vulnerable learners who may face additional barriers in second-language acquisition.

The intervention took place over two weeks in a Junior High School (Gymnasium) in Patras, Greece, with eight 15-year-old students in a German-as-a-foreign-language class. Students first wrote a personal email, then the researchers used ChatGPT to revise the texts specifically for vocabulary and grammar. Students received the improved version, discussed the revisions, and then wrote a second, similar email on a related topic intended to encourage transfer of the new language forms.

The study compared pre- and post-intervention texts using objective textual measures such as total words, unique words, and average words per sentence. Results showed increases on these measures for most students, suggesting that ChatGPT-supported feedback may help strengthen writing performance in this setting. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support language learning in multilingual classrooms, while also emphasizing the need for teacher supervision, critical checking of outputs, and further research in larger and more diverse contexts.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI language model/chatbot that generates and revises text from prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a feedback tool to improve students' foreign-language writing by correcting/enhancing vocabulary and grammar in their initial email drafts, with students then revising a similar writing task after reviewing the AI-improved version.

findings.finding_summary: In a pilot classroom study with 8 junior high school students (age 15) in a German-as-foreign-language class, ChatGPT-assisted revision was associated with longer and lexically richer post-intervention texts. The authors report increases in total words (mean increase 38%, ranging from 2% to 62%), unique words (mean 19.1 more per student, with one decrease), and average words per sentence (mean about 42%, with one student decreasing), but no inferential statistics were reported.
findings.measure: Total words, unique words, average words per sentence in students' pre- and post-intervention German emails

quality_tier_rationale: This is a small pilot classroom study with observational pre/post comparison and no control group or inferential testing reported. It provides implementation detail but limited causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported changes are moderate in magnitude at the text level (e.g., mean 38% increase in total words and about 42% increase in words per sentence). However, the evidence is based on a very small sample and descriptive analysis only.
